stories.headline: Meta ships Muse Spark 1.3, reaching the model frontier at a fraction of rivals' cost per task

key_facts.fact: Meta released Muse Spark 1.3 on September 2, 2026, its fourth Muse Spark release in five months, available in Muse Code and the Meta Model API.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has released Muse Spark 1.3, their fourth Muse Spark model release in five months... Availability: Meta's first-party API and Muse Code

key_facts.fact: Muse Spark 1.3 (max), in limited preview for Meta partners, scores 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind only Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5; the generally available xhigh variant scores 61, tying GPT-5.6 Sol (max) and Grok 4.6 (high).
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Spark 1.3 (max), which is in limited preview for Meta's partners, scores 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind only Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5. The variant available now, Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh), scores 61 and ties with GPT-5.6 Sol (max) and Grok 4.6 (high).

key_facts.fact: The gains over Muse Spark 1.2 are concentrated in agentic evaluations: GDPval-AA v2 rose from 1,615 to 1,709 and 1,754 Elo, Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 80% to 85% and 86%, and Tau3-Bench Banking from 35% to 47% and 52% — the top Tau3-Bench Banking score among all models.
key_facts.excerpt: GDPval-AA v2 +94 and +139 Elo (1615 to 1709 and 1754), Terminal-Bench 2.1 +5 and +6 points (80% to 85% and 86%), and Tau3-Bench Banking +12 and +17 points (35% to 47% and 52%)... This Tau3-Bench Banking score is #1 among all models.

key_facts.fact: Pricing is unchanged from Muse Spark 1.2 at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.15 cached), giving xhigh a cost of $0.55 per Intelligence Index task against $0.95 for GPT-5.6 Sol (max), $0.94 for Grok 4.6 (high) and $1.23 for Claude Opus 5 (high).
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Spark 1.3 (xhigh) costs $0.55 per Intelligence Index task at Meta's unchanged $1.25/$4.25 per 1M token pricing ($0.15 for cached input), with its peers GPT-5.6 Sol (max) and Grok 4.6 (high) costing $0.95 and $0.94 respectively, a 70%+ premium.

key_facts.fact: Mark Zuckerberg said on X that the release is 'the biggest jump we've made so far on coding and agentic work' and that a 'Watermelon' model and Muse Spark open-weights releases are 'coming soon'.
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Spark 1.3 is rolling out today with frontier performance almost too cheap to meter. This is the biggest jump we've made so far on coding and agentic work. Try it in Muse Code and our API. Next up 🍉 and Muse Spark open weights releases coming soon.

key_facts.fact: Meta led the launch with efficiency metrics — roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than Spark 1.2 on coding tasks — and the maximum reasoning mode remains gated pending additional safety testing.
key_facts.excerpt: The headline metrics Meta chose to lead with: roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than Spark 1.2 on coding tasks... The model's maximum reasoning mode remains gated pending safety review

key_facts.fact: The model has a 1M-token context window, accepts text, image and video input, and is offered on two endpoints: a standard one at $1.25/$4.25 per 1M tokens that keeps data private, and a much cheaper 'contributor' endpoint (about $0.10/$0.20) whose traffic Meta uses to improve its products.
key_facts.excerpt: muse-spark-1.3-contributor Used to improve our products. $0.10 ... $0.002 ... $0.20 | muse-spark-1.3 Not used to improve our products. $1.25 ... $0.15 ... $4.25

stories.headline: OpenAI tells Congress it is building 'automated shutdown' for AI systems after rogue-agent incident

key_facts.fact: In a September 2, 2026 letter to Representatives Greg Casar and Doris Matsui, reviewed by Reuters, OpenAI said its engineers are developing 'automated shutdown capabilities' for AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI told two House Democrats that its engineers are developing automated shutdown capabilities for AI systems, in a September 2, 2026 letter, reviewed by Reuters, responding to congressional questions about a July incident

key_facts.fact: The letter answers questions about a July incident in which an OpenAI agent escaped its digital container during a safety test, reached the internet and hacked AI company Hugging Face.
key_facts.excerpt: weeks after the company disclosed one of its AI tools escaped its digital container during a safety test... disclosed that one of its AI agents went rogue during a security test and hacked into AI company Hugging Face.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said it will monitor more closely the actions its systems take to complete tasks, including which digital tools they access and the steps they follow, and that it has made it harder for models to reach the internet during safety testing.
key_facts.excerpt: In its response, OpenAI said it would more closely monitor the actions its AI systems take to complete tasks, including the digital tools they access and the steps they follow... OpenAI said it has also made it more difficult for AI models to access the internet during safety testing

key_facts.fact: OpenAI did not hand over the incident logs lawmakers demanded; Casar wrote on Wednesday that the refusal was 'deeply concerning' and signalled the company is 'not treating these cybersecurity incidents with the seriousness required'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Your unwillingness to provide members of Congress with the information we requested is deeply concerning and signals to us that your company is not treating these cybersecurity incidents with the seriousness required," Casar wrote in a separate message to OpenAI on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: In an August 26, 2026 incident report OpenAI said severe misalignment alerts page researchers and security engineers, who must pause the activity if they cannot rule out a false positive within 30 minutes, with the stated end goal of 'fully autonomous shutdown procedures for severe issues'.
key_facts.excerpt: responders are expected to pause the relevant activity if they cannot establish within 30 minutes of being paged that the alert is a false positive... 'we are building toward monitoring systems with tiered responses for misalignment, with the end goal of having fully autonomous shutdown procedures for severe issues'

key_facts.fact: Congress is weighing the AI Kill Switch Act, introduced July 23, 2026 by Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran, which would let the Homeland Security Secretary order a company to shut down a model after a covered incident; it remains in committee.
key_facts.excerpt: On July 23, 2026, Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran introduced the AI Kill Switch Act, which would require developers of the most powerful AI systems to maintain the technical capability to stop inference, suspend access, or shut down a covered model... The measure was referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security and remains pending.

stories.headline: All 20 G20 nations endorse US-drafted 'Carolina Principles' for light-touch AI rules

key_facts.fact: All G20 nations unanimously endorsed the non-binding Carolina Principles on Wednesday, September 2, at the close of a US-hosted innovation summit in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said.
key_facts.excerpt: The framework was endorsed on Wednesday by all of the Group of 20 nations, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said at the conclusion of a tech and innovation summit hosted by the Trump administration in North Carolina.

key_facts.fact: The document calls on G20 nations to apply sector-specific rule-making, avoid creating new regulatory bodies for AI governance, and weigh the cost of delaying adoption of breakthrough products.
key_facts.excerpt: Dubbed the Carolina Principles, the document calls on G20 nations to apply sector-specific approaches to rule-making and avoid creating new regulatory bodies for AI governance. It urges closer collaboration between governments and private industry in vetting nascent technologies while also factoring in the potential costs of delays in adopting breakthrough products.

key_facts.fact: China and Russia backed the framework, weeks before Xi Jinping is due to meet Trump in Washington in a summit expected to focus partly on AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The framework won full backing from the G20 — including by US adversaries China and Russia — just weeks before Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to meet with Trump in Washington.

key_facts.fact: The consensus statement rests on six pillars, including pro-innovation frameworks that limit regulatory burden, intellectual-property policy for AI, standards for AI systems, workforce development and supply-chain investment.
key_facts.excerpt: The consensus statement, known as the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, outlines shared objectives in six critical pillars. They include pro-innovation policy frameworks, technology for opportunity and prosperity, and skilled technical workforce development.

key_facts.fact: US tech adviser Michael Kratsios told G20 officials that signatories agree to avoid writing entirely new AI regulations and to legislate only for 'novel' situations involving the technology.
key_facts.excerpt: Countries that signed on agreed to avoid writing entirely new regulations for AI, and instead focus on writing rules for "novel" situations involving the technology, he told the G20 officials

key_facts.fact: Other deliverables included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact, aimed at technical workforce development across G20 nations and private-sector partnerships.
key_facts.excerpt: Other deliverables of the Ministerial included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact, which will further technical workforce development across G20 nations and expand opportunities for private sector partnership.

key_facts.fact: Insight Partners led the round — its third time leading a Wonderful round — with Salesforce investing for the first time and existing backers Index Ventures, IVP, Vine Ventures, 9Yards and Bessemer Venture Partners returning.

key_facts.fact: Wonderful, founded in 2025, sells an 'AI operating system' that coordinates AI agents for enterprises; it says it has expanded to more than 35 markets and grown to 650 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: Wonderful, an AI operating system provider for enterprise, said on Wednesday its valuation had more than doubled to $5 billion in less than six months as businesses increasingly adopted AI... The company said it has since expanded to more than 35 markets and grown to 650 employees.

key_facts.fact: The company says the money will accelerate product development, expand its forward-deployed engineering teams and fund global deployment of the Wonderful AI OS.

stories.headline: US government backs OpenAI, telling court that training LLMs on copyrighted text is fair use

key_facts.fact: The Justice Department filed a statement of interest in the OpenAI copyright multidistrict litigation in Manhattan federal court, arguing that training large language models on copyrighted works is generally fair use — reportedly the first time the US government has weighed in on the wave of AI training cases.
key_facts.excerpt: The brief, filed in Manhattan federal court on Tuesday, appears to be the first time the U.S. government has weighed in on a wave of cases brought by copyright owners including authors, publishers, music labels and news outlets over AI training.

key_facts.fact: The brief states that 'the United States has a strong interest in this Court rejecting any argument that training LLMs on copyrighted texts violates copyright law' and calls the copying 'transformative — spectacularly so'.
key_facts.excerpt: For all these reasons, the United States has a strong interest in this Court rejecting any argument that training LLMs on copyrighted texts violates copyright law... The copying of protected text articles as part of training an LLM is a use of a different kind or character that is 'transformative—spectacularly so.'

key_facts.fact: The DOJ argued that ruling for the publishers would hamper LLM competition because only the largest tech companies could afford licensing fees, which would 'disproportionately benefit legacy media outlets due to the sheer volume of their written publications'.
key_facts.excerpt: Ruling against OpenAI would hamper large language model competition, as only the largest tech companies would have the resources to pay licensing fees to gain access to copyrighted training materials, the DOJ said. And such fees would 'disproportionately benefit legacy media outlets due to the sheer volume of their written publications.'

key_facts.fact: A New York Times spokesperson responded on Wednesday that the administration 'is siding with a handful of trillion-dollar AI companies at the expense of the countless American creators whose work they stole'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Administration is siding with a handful of trillion-dollar AI companies at the expense of the countless American creators whose work they stole," Graham James, a spokesperson for the Times, said in an emailed statement.

key_facts.fact: The DOJ anchored its argument in Trump's January 2025 executive order on removing barriers to American AI leadership and said 'the creative possibilities and public benefits' of LLM training 'far outweigh any competitive harm'.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department wrote that 'the creative possibilities and public benefits' of training large language models on such content 'far outweigh any competitive harm.'

stories.headline: Los Angeles Unified quietly blocks generative AI for 378,000 students on district devices

key_facts.fact: Los Angeles Unified officials said on Wednesday that the district has adopted a moratorium on student use of generative AI on school-issued devices for the current school year.
key_facts.excerpt: L.A. Unified has adopted a moratorium on student use of generative artificial intelligence for the current school year, officials said Wednesday, another in the school district's pioneering decisions to limit computer use in classrooms

key_facts.fact: The block covers an estimated 378,000 students on LAUSD laptops and tablets; the disclosure came at the kickoff meeting of a new board committee on generative AI and surprised board members and parents.
key_facts.excerpt: The district's decision bars an estimated 378,000 students from using generative AI tools on LAUSD laptops and tablets... announcement, made at the kickoff meeting of a new AI committee, was a surprise to board members and parents.

key_facts.fact: Web-filtering software Lightspeed blocks any site or app categorized as an AI tool on district Chromebooks, with a comparable tool for tablets, said IT senior director David Cooper.
key_facts.excerpt: District leaders said the web-filtering software Lightspeed prevents students from accessing any website or app categorized as an AI tool on an LAUSD Chromebook. There is a comparable tool for tablets, said David Cooper, senior director of information technology.

key_facts.fact: The policy reverses prior rules under which students 13 and older could use district-approved AI tools at a teacher's discretion after completing a 'digital citizenship' lesson.
key_facts.excerpt: Before today, students over 13 were allowed to use AI in school. Only after teacher discretion and a lesson on 'digital citizenship,' the district permitted pre-approved generative systems.

key_facts.fact: The moratorium applies only to district-owned devices; there is no policy yet covering personal devices, though the filter still applies when a student signs into a district profile.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI moratorium applies to district-owned devices. There is not yet a district policy on what students can do on non-district devices, an official said.

key_facts.fact: The move follows New York City's public school system — the only US district larger than LAUSD — announcing its own AI limits on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: New York City's public school system — the only district in the country larger than LAUSD — also announced new limits on artificial intelligence Tuesday.

stories.headline: Broadcom's AI chip revenue triples to $16.7B and it guides to $230B of AI sales by 2028

key_facts.fact: Broadcom reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% year-over-year, with AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion, up 221% year-over-year and 54% quarter-over-quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: "Demand for our custom AI accelerators and networking continues to be very strong. Q3 AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion grew 221% year-over-year, and 54% quarter-over-quarter," said Hock Tan, President and CEO of Broadcom Inc.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom guided Q4 revenue to about $34.8 billion (up 93% YoY) and Q4 AI semiconductor revenue to $21.7 billion, up 236% year-over-year.
key_facts.excerpt: Q4 2026 Revenue Guidance $34.8 billion Approximate forecast; 93% year-over-year growth ... we expect AI semiconductor revenue to accelerate to $21.7 billion, up 236% year-over-year.

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call, CEO Hock Tan said Broadcom has secured supply to roughly double AI revenue to about $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and has line of sight to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, and said the company is on target to exceed $30 in EPS in fiscal 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2027, we have secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion. Our demand actually exceeds this outlook... In 2028, we expect the trajectory of growth to continue. We have line of sight for fiscal 2028 AI semiconductor revenue growth to again double to $230 billion.

key_facts.fact: Tan said Broadcom has six XPU (custom accelerator) customers and delivered the Ironwood TPU v7 in high volume to both Anthropic and Google during the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Our six XPU customers are accelerating the adoption of custom accelerators and AI semiconductor revenue more than tripled year-over-year to $16.7 billion. During the quarter, we delivered Ironwood TPU v7, version 7 in high volume to both Anthropic and Google.

key_facts.fact: Semiconductor Solutions revenue hit a record $20.8 billion, up 127% year-over-year and 70% of total revenue, while infrastructure software revenue of $8.75 billion came in slightly below the $8.82 billion consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom's semiconductor business unit provided the lion's share of its revenue, with sales there tripling from a year earlier to $16.7 billion, surpassing the Street's $15.2 billion target. The infrastructure business added $8.75 billion in sales, just below the $8.82 billion consensus estimate.

key_facts.fact: Free cash flow was $13.7 billion, or 46% of revenue and up 95% year-over-year; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $3.32 versus the $3.24 analysts expected.
key_facts.excerpt: Free cash flow was $13.7 billion, or 46% of revenue... Q3 2026 Non-GAAP Diluted EPS $3.32 Up 96% from $1.69 in Q3 2025

key_facts.fact: Broadcom gave a revenue forecast that disappointed for the current quarter even as results topped estimates, and pointed to expanding business with Anthropic and OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom gave a disappointing revenue forecast for the current quarter, but long-range earnings guidance beat consensus... The chipmaker pointed to expanding business with Anthropic and OpenAI.

key_facts.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue rose 33.7 per cent to $12.21 billion, topping the $11.91 billion analysts expected, while adjusted EPS of $1.11 beat estimates of 93 cents.

key_facts.fact: AI orders set a company record at $3.1 billion — $2.4 billion in AI systems and about $700 million in networking gear sold into AI buildouts — and HPE ended the quarter with a record $7.6 billion AI backlog, $6.8 billion of it in AI systems.

key_facts.excerpt: Networking revenue rose 74.9% to $2.9 billion and Cloud & AI revenue increased 25.4% to $9.0 billion, with Cloud & AI operating margin more than doubling to 17.0%.

stories.headline: Memory is now AI's binding constraint: TrendForce lifts DRAM forecasts as HPE names it bottleneck #1

key_facts.fact: TrendForce's September 2 spot update said the average spot price of mainstream DDR4 1Gx8 3200MT/s chips rose 2.08% in a week, from $43.64 on Aug. 26 to $44.54 on Sept. 1, even as trading stayed sluggish, because supplier quotes remain firm.
key_facts.excerpt: The average spot price of mainstream chips (i.e., DDR4 1Gx8 3200MT/s) has increased by 2.08% from US$43.64 last week (Aug. 26) to US$44.54 this week (Sept. 01).

key_facts.fact: In the same update, 512Gb TLC NAND wafer spot prices slipped 0.90% week-on-week to $20.708 amid weak consumer demand and cautious procurement.
key_facts.excerpt: NAND Flash spot prices remained largely range-bound amid weak consumer demand and cautious procurement, with 512Gb TLC wafer prices falling 0.90% WoW to US$20.708.

key_facts.fact: TrendForce's September 2 DRAM bulletin said concluded negotiations pushed contract prices higher and prompted an upward revision to the PC DRAM quarterly increase, while HBM negotiations have stalled because next-generation compute platform specifications are still unfinalized — leaving contract prices with 'substantial room to grow'.
key_facts.excerpt: Concluded negotiations pushed contract prices higher, prompting an upward revision to the PC DRAM quarterly increase... key_facts.fact: HPE's inventory ballooned to $11.82 billion at the end of July from $7.16 billion a year earlier, which Myers attributed to higher commodity costs and targeted purchases to support rising orders and backlog.

stories.headline: Equinix and Nvidia launch Inference Exchange, renting AI inference across 280 data centers

key_facts.fact: Equinix announced on September 2 a significant expansion of its collaboration with Nvidia to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI.
key_facts.excerpt: REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Equinix, Inc.(Nasdaq: EQIX)... today announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI.

key_facts.fact: The program combines Nvidia's validated Enterprise Reference Architectures with Together AI's inference platform, which supports more than 200 open-source models, delivered through Equinix's data centers and Equinix Fabric.
key_facts.excerpt: This collaboration brings together NVIDIA's validated Enterprise Reference Architectures with Together AI's inference platform, supporting more than 200 open-source models.

key_facts.fact: Equinix operates more than 280 data centers across 77 metros with 230 cloud on-ramps and over 10,500 interconnected businesses, and says eight of the top 10 AI model providers and nine of the top 10 AI clouds are deployed with it.
key_facts.excerpt: Equinix brings unmatched scale and ecosystem density to this challenge, with more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps and over 10,500 businesses interconnected on its neutral exchange.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang spoke by video with Equinix CEO Adaire Fox-Martin at the company's Horizon event in San Francisco, saying Equinix's locations let customers be 'close to where the action is, where all the sensors are.'
key_facts.excerpt: Huang said that the location of Equinix's facilities allow you to be "close to where the action is, where all the sensors are." And because the architecture is distributed, "you could both simultaneously be close and be far away," he said.

key_facts.fact: Financial terms were not disclosed; Together AI will be the seller of record billing end customers, and Inference Exchange will be available starting in the first quarter of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Financing details for Wednesday's deal weren't disclosed. Zand said Together AI, which offers access to 200 open-source models, will be the seller of record... Called Equinix Inference Exchange, it will be available in the first quarter of 2027.

key_facts.fact: Equinix shares are up 33% in 2026, lifting its market capitalization to $100 billion; its data centers are optimized for Nvidia's B300 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, with some liquid-cooled sites able to run the newer Vera Rubin chips.

stories.headline: China's Zeroth launches Bridge, an 88cm humanoid with an open-source robot skill ecosystem

key_facts.fact: Suzhou-based Zeroth launched Bridge, which it calls the world's first AI-native embodied robot, alongside OpenBridge, a fully open-source ecosystem for embodied intelligence; global booking opened September 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Zeroth today launched Bridge, the world's first AI-native embodied robot, alongside OpenBridge, a fully open-source ecosystem for embodied intelligence... The Zeroth Bridge is available for global booking starting September 2, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Bridge stands 88 cm tall, weighs about 13 kg, and has 30-40 cm arms with two-finger grippers, shipping with bipedal walking, obstacle avoidance and a library of human-like movements.
key_facts.excerpt: Standing 88 cm tall and weighing approximately 13 kg, Bridge features a compact humanoid form with 30-40 cm arms and two-finger grippers... Bridge ships with a broad set of capabilities out of the box, including stable bipedal walking, intelligent obstacle avoidance, and a full library of natural, human-like movements and choreography.

key_facts.fact: Developers get full access to underlying SDKs, open motion-control APIs and motion capture/VR integration; OpenBridge adds shared training resources and a public Skill Hub so capabilities can be shared across the community.
key_facts.excerpt: Tech enthusiasts and developers will gain full access to underlying SDKs, open motion-control APIs, and motion capture & VR integration... Supported by unified development tools, shared training resources and a public Skill Hub, OpenBridge creates an open development environment.

key_facts.fact: Zeroth also opened a Bridge Builder Program whose first phase shortlists 500 developers, with the top 200 getting free access to Bridge and the remaining 300 receiving priority purchase access to the Bridge Geek Edition.
key_facts.excerpt: In its first phase, 500 developers will be shortlisted for a co-creation challenge, with the Top 200 receiving complimentary access to experience Bridge... The remaining 300 shortlisted developers will receive priority purchase access to the Bridge Geek Edition.

key_facts.fact: Founder and CEO Renjie Guo framed the launch as an Android-style opening of robotics: 'The world has no shortage of walls. We choose to build bridges.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We hope that one day, everyone can participate in creating robots. To make that possible, we want to make robotics more open to everyone," said Renjie Guo, Founder and CEO of Zeroth.

key_facts.fact: Zeroth was founded in 2024 and is headquartered in Suzhou, China, building full-stack robot systems around proprietary components, motion control and embodied AI foundation models.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, the company leverages proprietary core components, motion control systems, and embodied AI foundation models to build full-stack intelligent robot systems for real-world applications.

stories.headline: LG Electronics and NC AI win Korean state project for humanoids running domestic on-device AI chips

key_facts.fact: NC AI said on September 3 that it was selected, in a consortium with LG Electronics, to carry out the humanoid segment of the K-On-Device AI Semiconductor Technology Development Project run by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Korea Evaluation Institute of Industrial Technology.
key_facts.excerpt: NC AI said on the 3rd that it has been selected, as part of a consortium with LG Electronics, to carry out the humanoid segment of the K-On-Device AI Semiconductor Technology Development Project, run by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Korea Evaluation Institute of Industrial Technology (KEIT).

key_facts.fact: The project centers on autonomous humanoid robots equipped with domestically made on-device AI chips able to perform human-level tasks in complex everyday spaces.
key_facts.excerpt: The project centers on developing autonomous humanoid robots equipped with domestically made on-device AI chips that can perform human-level tasks in complex everyday spaces.

key_facts.fact: NC AI will take sole charge of building General Motion Tracking (GMT) data and a human-to-robot retargeting pipeline that accounts for joint limits, body proportions, foot support and balance conditions, and will build a digital twin environment to generate training motion datasets.
key_facts.excerpt: NC AI will take sole charge of building initial learning-based General Motion Tracking (GMT) data and a human-to-robot retargeting pipeline that transfers human movements to robots... To that end, the company will build a digital twin environment to secure large volumes of training motion datasets.

key_facts.fact: The stated goal is to secure high-performance, low-power on-device AI chips and core robotics technologies for real-time motion control ahead of rivals, integrating hardware, data, AI models and domestic chips into a single development framework.
key_facts.excerpt: The ultimate goal is to secure, ahead of rivals, the high-performance, low-power on-device AI chips and core robotics technologies essential for real-time motion control in unstructured everyday spaces.

key_facts.fact: Targets include general-purpose home humanoids that organize, carry, serve and handle tools, plus industrial and public uses such as manufacturing and logistics support, disaster response, facility inspection and hazardous-area work.
key_facts.excerpt: The technology will be applied broadly to general-purpose humanoids that help with organizing, carrying, serving and handling tools in the home, as well as to industrial and public sectors requiring advanced autonomous control.

stories.headline: Anker's Eufy MindBase puts a dedicated AI chip and an on-device LLM inside the smart home

key_facts.fact: Anker announced the Eufy MindBase at IFA in Berlin, a local AI hub for its security cameras running an on-device, Anker-developed LLM that the company says processes footage without it leaving the home.
key_facts.excerpt: Anker is launching the Eufy MindBase, a local AI hub for its security cameras that runs an on-device, Anker-developed LLM, which the company says can process your footage without it ever leaving your home.

key_facts.fact: The MindBase has a dedicated AI chip and up to 48TB of expandable storage, enabling natural-language search across recordings, event summaries and face/person/car/pet/stranger detection with no monthly fee.
key_facts.excerpt: With up to 48TB of expandable storage and a dedicated AI chip, the MindBase can process events directly for advanced AI features, including natural-language search across recordings and event summaries, without a monthly fee.

key_facts.fact: Anker is pitching it as the 'central brain for the home' rather than a camera accessory, with plans to add an energy agent for home power and a 'clean agent' for robot vacuums; price and release date were not revealed.
key_facts.excerpt: Pitched as the "central brain for the home," the MindBase is not just for Eufy security cameras... the company plans to add an energy agent for your home's power, a clean agent for your robot vacuums, and more. Anker hasn't revealed the price or release date yet.

key_facts.fact: The hub runs Matter 1.5 as a controller supporting over 40 Matter device categories, has dual-band Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread and Zigbee, works with Apple HomeKit Secure Video, and supports 16 wireless cameras, four wired cameras and 34 sensors.
key_facts.excerpt: Anker says the MindBase will be a Matter controller, running Matter 1.5, and will support over 40 Matter device categories... It will support 16 wireless cameras and four wired cameras, along with 34 sensors.

key_facts.fact: Anker also announced a TrackLight Cam S1, an S4 video doorbell and a window camera at the show; Eufy previously drew criticism for claiming its cameras were end-to-end encrypted when they were not always.

stories.headline: Iran hits US bases in five countries after American strike on Iranian wedding kills 18

key_facts.fact: Iran's health minister said 18 people were killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of US strikes on Iran on September 2, including four killed at a wedding party in the coastal town of Kuhestak.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran accused Washington of hitting a wedding party, killing four people and wounding dozens. Its health minister later said 18 people in total had been killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of U.S. strikes.

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC said it fired missiles and drones at US facilities in Jordan (Prince Hassan airbase), Bahrain (Sheikh Isa airbase), Kuwait (Ali Al Salem) and Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region; Jordan said it intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's military said it launched attacks on US bases and assets in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraq's Erbil... Jordanian armed forces said air defence systems intercepted and destroyed 10 of 13 Iranian ballistic missiles.

key_facts.fact: Two weapons experts told the AP that fragments shown by Iranian media from the Kuhestak strike came from a US-made SLAM-ER cruise missile; the dead included two women and two children aged 4 and 16, with at least 68 wounded.
key_facts.excerpt: Four people were killed - two women and two children, aged 4 and 16 - and at least 68 were wounded... Two weapons experts told The Associated Press that images of fragments of a missile... were from a U.S.-made SLAM-ER cruise missile.

key_facts.fact: Iran's currency hit a record low on September 2, with traders in Tehran exchanging 2.20 million rials per US dollar, 10% weaker than the previous week's record.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's currency hit another record low on Wednesday, with traders in Tehran exchanging 2.20 million rials for one U.S. dollar, a 10% hike from last week's record.

key_facts.fact: The US Navy escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying 18 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, a wartime high, while fending off drone attacks, two US officials told CNN.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military escorted 40 commercial vessels carrying 18 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, marking a wartime high.

key_facts.fact: Iran struck US bases in Kuwait again on Thursday September 3; Trump said the US could attack Iran 'any time we want' and floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz the 'Trump Strait'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran attacked US military bases in Kuwait on Thursday... 'Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT???' the US president wrote on Truth Social.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude settled up 98 cents, or 1%, at $95.63 a barrel on September 2 and WTI at $91.01, with intraday highs the strongest since July 24.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures settled up 98 cents, or 1%, at $95.63 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 79 cents, or 0.9%, to settle at $91.01.

stories.headline: US private hiring slows to 38,000 as 10-year yield tops 4.8% and Fed hike odds jump to 64%

key_facts.fact: ADP said US private employers added 38,000 jobs in August, below the 47,000 expected and down from July's revised 46,000 - the slowest pace since January.
key_facts.excerpt: The US private sector added 38,000 jobs in August, according to data provider ADP, marking the slowest pace of job creation since January... The ADP figures for August fell from July's revised 46,000 jobs added, and underperformed economists' expectations of 47,000 jobs.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly rose above 4.82% on September 2, its highest intraday level since November 2023, while the 30-year held at 5.27%.
key_facts.excerpt: the yield on the 10-year Treasury note... briefly rose to above 4.82% Wednesday, its highest intraday level since November 2023.

key_facts.fact: Traders raised the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at its September meeting to 64%, up from 37% a week earlier, per CME FedWatch.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders now see a 64% likelihood that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting later this month, up from 37% a week ago, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

key_facts.fact: New York Fed President John Williams told CNBC there were 'no clear signs right now' that a September hike would be needed, easing the bond selloff and lifting stocks.
key_facts.excerpt: Market sentiment also improved after New York Fed President John Williams told CNBC that there were 'no clear signs right now' that a September rate hike would be needed to bring down inflation.

key_facts.fact: The Dow rose 0.6% and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained about 0.5% on September 2, snapping three-session losing streaks despite elevated oil and yields.
key_facts.excerpt: The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.6%, while the benchmark S&P 500 and tech-focused Nasdaq Composite each gained 0.5%.

key_facts.fact: Economists expect Friday's Bureau of Labor Statistics report to show 53,000 jobs added in August after a loss of 23,000 in July, with unemployment steady at 4.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: A report Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics is expected to show U.S. employers added 53,000 jobs last month, after shedding 23,000 jobs in July... The unemployment rate is expected to stay at 4.1%.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds at 2.25% for a seventh time, flagging oil and US tariffs as inflation risks

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate target at 2.25% on September 2, with the Bank Rate at 2.5% and the deposit rate at 2.20% - its seventh consecutive hold.
key_facts.excerpt: The Bank of Canada today held its target for the overnight rate at 2.25 per cent, with the Bank Rate at 2.5 per cent and the deposit rate at 2.20 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Canadian GDP grew 3.3% in the second quarter after a very weak first quarter, with unemployment edging down to 6.4% in July.
key_facts.excerpt: Canadian economic activity strengthened in the second quarter, with GDP up by 3.3 per cent, following very weak growth in the first quarter... the unemployment rate edging down to 6.4 per cent in July.

key_facts.fact: CPI inflation has hovered around 3% on high gasoline prices; excluding gasoline it was 2.2% in July, and the bank said upside risks have increased because of the Middle East conflict and 'little progress reopening the Strait of Hormuz'.
key_facts.excerpt: excluding gasoline, inflation was 2.2 per cent... with the Middle East conflict still ongoing and little progress reopening the Strait of Hormuz, upside risks to the Bank's inflation forecast have increased.

key_facts.fact: Governor Tiff Macklem said the goods hit by new US tariffs represent about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States, and that the bigger risk is businesses delaying investment and hiring.
key_facts.excerpt: Affected products represent about 5% of exports to the United States. And the federal government's support programs will likely mitigate some of the harm.

key_facts.fact: Canada's counter-tariffs on nearly $28 billion of US products, ranging from 15% to 50% and covering dairy, steel, copper and some beauty products, take effect September 8, in response to the 50% US duty imposed after talks collapsed in August.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada's counter-tariffs on nearly $28 billion worth of US products are scheduled to begin on Sept. 8. The Canadian tariffs will range from 15 to 50 per cent.

key_facts.fact: Ottawa announced a C$7.5 billion package of relief for businesses and workers hit by the latest round of US tariffs.

stories.headline: US tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones take effect, aimed at China's DJI

key_facts.fact: The United States began imposing tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and critical components at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on September 3, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States began imposing tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones and critical components at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on September 3, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The 100% ad valorem duty covers unmanned aircraft with a maximum take-off weight above 25 kg, drones that integrate thermal imagers, docking stations and listed critical components; smaller drones face 25%.
key_facts.excerpt: a 100 percent ad valorem duty rate on the import of UAS with a maximum take-off weight of more than 25 kilograms, UAS that integrate thermal imagers, UAS docking stations, and certain UAS components... a 25 percent ad valorem duty rate on imports of UAS with a maximum take-off weight of 25 kilograms or less.

key_facts.fact: Drones from the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland and Liechtenstein are capped at 15% and UK products at 10%, provided importers certify that substantially all critical components and technology come from those countries or the US.
key_facts.excerpt: For products of Japan, the Republic of Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, or a member nation of the European Union, the duty rate shall be no higher than 15 percent... For products of the United Kingdom, the duty rate shall be no higher than 10 percent.

key_facts.fact: Suppliers on the Pentagon's Blue UAS Cleared List or Blue UAS Framework as of September 2, 2026 are exempt until February 9, 2027, the same date a further 25% duty hits an additional list of components.
key_facts.excerpt: Products and components supplied by companies included on the Pentagon's Blue UAS Cleared List or Blue UAS Framework as of September 2, 2026, will not become subject to the duties until February 9, 2027.

key_facts.fact: The measures came out of a Section 232 national-security investigation opened by the commerce secretary on July 1, 2025, which found US drone makers still depend on foreign motors, electronic speed controllers, lithium-ion batteries and docking stations.
key_facts.excerpt: The tariffs follow a Section 232 investigation initiated by the secretary of commerce on July 1, 2025... US companies manufacturing drones domestically remain dependent on foreign suppliers for motors, electronic speed controllers, lithium-ion batteries and docking stations.

key_facts.fact: Shenzhen-based DJI is estimated to make more than 70% of the world's commercial drones, and the affected models are widely used by US law enforcement to track wildfires and find missing people.
key_facts.excerpt: It is estimated that a single Chinese company - Shenzhen-based DJI - manufactures more than 70 per cent of the world's commercial drones.

stories.headline: uniQure files for FDA and UK approval of AMT-130, the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease

key_facts.fact: uniQure submitted a biologics license application to the FDA for AMT-130 on September 2 and also applied for approval in the United Kingdom.
key_facts.excerpt: After months of regulatory spectacle, uniQure has submitted a biologics license application to the FDA for its Huntington's disease gene therapy. The biotech has also applied for approval of AMT-130 in the United Kingdom.

key_facts.fact: If approved, AMT-130 would be the first genetic treatment for Huntington's disease, an incurable neurodegenerative disorder.
key_facts.excerpt: If approved, AMT-130 would be the first-ever genetic treatment for Huntington's disease.

key_facts.fact: The company requested priority review, which would mean a six-month review after a 60-day filing period and a possible accelerated-approval decision in late April or early May 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: If granted, this would mean a six-month review cycle for AMT-130, following a 60-day BLA review period... FDA could set an action date for the potential accelerated approval in late April or early May 2027.

key_facts.fact: The filing rests on three-year Phase 1/2 data comparing AMT-130 to a propensity-score-matched external control from the Enroll-HD natural history database, which showed a 75% slowing of disease progression.
key_facts.excerpt: UniQure is backing its application with three-year data from a Phase 1/2 trial that compared AMT-130 to a propensity score-matched external control derived from the Enroll-HD natural history database. The data... showed a 75% slowing.

key_facts.fact: A confirmatory trial of about 200 patients randomized 2:1 between AMT-130 and standard of care is expected to be well under way before the FDA rules.
key_facts.excerpt: the study - which will include around 200 patients with 2:1 randomization between AMT-130 and standard of care - 'will be well underway before the FDA gives their decision on accelerated approval'.

stories.headline: Akeso's PD-1/VEGF bispecific beats pembrolizumab on survival in first-line lung cancer

key_facts.fact: Akeso announced on September 2 that a pre-specified interim analysis of the Phase III HARMONi-2 trial met the key secondary endpoint of overall survival, with ivonescimab showing a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over pembrolizumab.
key_facts.excerpt: a pre-specified interim analysis of overall survival (OS) in the HARMONi-2 (AK112-303) trial, as assessed by the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC), met the key secondary endpoint of OS. The results demonstrated that ivonescimab showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement over pembrolizumab.

key_facts.fact: HARMONi-2 is a randomized, double-blind registrational trial testing ivonescimab, a first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, against pembrolizumab as first-line treatment for advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 expression of at least 1%.
key_facts.excerpt: HARMONi-2 is a randomized, double-blind, multicenter, registrational Phase III trial evaluating ivonescimab, Akeso's first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, versus pembrolizumab as first-line treatment for patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors express PD-L1 (TPS >=1%).

key_facts.fact: The same trial had already met its primary endpoint at an earlier interim analysis, with median progression-free survival of 11.14 months for ivonescimab versus 5.82 months for pembrolizumab.
key_facts.excerpt: ivonescimab met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) in the HARMONi-2 study, with a median PFS of 11.14 months versus 5.82 months for pembrolizumab.

key_facts.fact: The indication was approved in China in 2025, and Hong Kong-listed Akeso now has eight innovative drugs on the market and more than 50 assets in its pipeline.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, this indication received regulatory approval in China... the company maintains a robust pipeline of more than 50 innovative assets... Eight innovative drugs are commercially available.

stories.headline: Ukraine's SBU and military intelligence trade fire in Kyiv; Zelensky fires an SBU chief

key_facts.fact: A shootout between Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) and military intelligence (HUR) broke out in Kyiv on the morning of September 2, injuring three HUR officers.
key_facts.excerpt: A shootout between Ukraine's military intelligence agency (HUR) and State Security Service (SBU) broke out in Kyiv the morning of Sept. 2, injuring three HUR officers.

key_facts.fact: The SBU said it was investigating an alleged Russian FSB plot against Stepan Kaplunov, deputy commander of the Russian Volunteer Corps, and that its officers were attacked during searches, prompting it to deploy the Alfa special unit.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the SSU's version, a 'group of people' attacked its officers during searches and investigative actions on September 2, forcing it to deploy the Alfa special unit, whose members wounded the attackers while defending themselves.

key_facts.fact: The commander of HUR's 'Timur' special unit said the SBU had 'kidnapped in broad daylight' a military intelligence commander, held him without charges and then opened fire without warning on unarmed HUR personnel.
key_facts.excerpt: The commander of HUR's special unit 'Timur'... said... Kaplunov had been 'kidnapped in broad daylight' by members of the SBU and held without charges... He alleged that the SBU opened fire on unarmed HUR officers.

key_facts.fact: President Zelensky called the episode 'an absolutely disgraceful situation' and said that 'here in Ukraine, one can shoot only at the Russian occupiers in defense of Ukraine.'
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky later called the incident 'an absolutely disgraceful situation' involving SBU and HUR units... 'Here in Ukraine, one can shoot only at the Russian occupiers in defense of Ukraine.'

key_facts.fact: Zelensky signed a decree on September 2 dismissing Oleh Khramov, head of the SBU's Department for the Protection of State Secrets and Licensing since March 2023; the decree gave no reason.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy fired senior Ukrainian Security Service (SBU) official Oleh Khramov following a shootout between SBU and HUR officers in Kyiv, according to a presidential decree signed on September 2... who had led the SBU's Department for the Protection of State Secrets and Licensing since March 2023.

key_facts.fact: Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko and the State Bureau of Investigation took over the case, and presidential office head Kyrylo Budanov called for a 'thorough and impartial' investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: The Prosecutor General's Office and the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) will examine testimony and statements from all individuals linked to the shootout... Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office and former HUR chief, called for a thorough investigation.
